rows.claim: `match` now strips trailing slashes from the path before comparing, so `/users/42/` matches `/users/{id}` and returns `{"id": "42"}`.
rows.evidence: The edit added `path = path.rstrip("/") or "/"`. The post-fix pytest run shows test_trailing_slash no longer fails (only test_unknown_method_is_404 fails, 6 passed), and that test asserts match("/users/{id}", "/users/42/") == {"id": "42"}.

No tool output tests a bare "/" path. No test covers it and the agent never ran such a case. The code's `or "/"` fallback suggests intent, but with pattern "/" the pattern is stripped to "" and split gives [""], while path "/" split gives [""] after [1:], so it would likely work, yet this was not verified by any output.
